description: Exact-target facts for the rematch wrapper (V4 balance493 EN/IT, identical bytes in both languages). Everything here was read back from the ARM9 images; runtime context is the one exception and is marked UNPROVEN.

seam.note: BL to TrainerData_ReadTrPoke: after the archive member is loaded into the transient buffer and before the first species/override is interpreted (type-3 loop starts at 0x02073694)

loader.note: thunk: r0=trainer id, r1=buffer; tail-calls the archive reader with (buffer, 0x38, trainer id)

host_frame.note: offsets from the host SP at the seam (after the host prologue, before any wrapper push)

plus_byte.evidence: read as ldrb [0x023D8700] by the Plus level function at 0x023D8134 (literal at 0x023D818C); contract active_plus

context.note: The two values are the battleType built by SetupAndStartTrainerBattle for the phone entry (a4 = 0) and for the inherited Dojo sequence (a4 = 1); both measured by executing the real V4 function. Any other value, including every extra bit, stays native. The value actually seen at runtime is the Android capture's job (context proof); enemy party index 1 is a reference-source value.

phone.script: a/0/1/2 member 832, TrainerBattle at 0x41F (713) and 0x4D9 (712), a4 = 0

dojo-sequence.script: a/0/1/2 member 832, inherited sequence TrainerBattle at 0x706 (712) and 0x738 (713), a4 = 1

seed_policy: selector reads the host's saved pre-construction seed [sp+0x68]; no RNG call, no write; the constructor restores it at 0x02073A8E

tm_table.note: u16 move ids TM01..TM92, HM01..HM08 (pret item.c sTMHMMoves order); used only to prove legality of authored sets

setup.note: SetupAndStartTrainerBattle (whole function with its literal pool). Single trainer: battleType = 1 (BATTLE_TYPE_TRAINER) | 0x800 (BATTLE_TYPE_11) when the stack argument a4 is non-zero (movs r4,#1; cmp a4,#0; lsls r0,r4,#0xb; orrs r4,r0 at 0x020513A2..0x020513AA). Doubles 0x3, tag 0x13 and multi 0x4B are other values. Executed on the real bytes by the tests.

overlay.note: The module is loaded on demand: overlay 126 is a placeholder of the V4 (a 20-byte compressed file never loaded by the game). The installer rewrites its y9 row (window, size, uncompressed) and appends the module image as its file; a resident stub in c8.module-stubs loads it with HandleLoadOverlay, calls it and unloads it in the same call.
overlay.conflicts_note: CanOverlayBeLoaded refuses a window that touches a registered overlay; from 0x0226A920 up the window overlaps only overlay 12 (the battle), where HandleLoadOverlay returns 0 and the stub runs the native reader.

stub.note: push {r0,r1,r4,lr}: the module is entered with the host's r0/r1 and an extra 16-byte frame, which the hook adds to its host-SP offset.
